queue.brief: THE BET. Expect and welcome a 150-300 line diff; this is not a polish job. Measured on HEAD this pass (seed 42, warp 625): the courtyard's paved annulus between the ring bed and the edge beds is 1,896 PATH cells running r 13.8 to 37.8 off the linden — 15.6% of the world's 12,144 cells, the largest single-tile ground surface in the town, against the plaza's 730 PATH and the river's 920 WATER. Everything standing on it is four BENCH_SPOTS. The plaza, a third the size, carries a fountain, a roundel, pits, six benches, six fount stands, two crumb spots, a rail, five bollards and a fourteen-place door. Give the courtyard a COVERED WALK: an arcade along the inside face of one range of the surrounding block, so that the garden has a roofed edge you can be under. The recommended shape is the one GLASS (#116) and LEADS (#170) already proved — a tile of its own with its own fill in the ground cache, so that the floor reads as roofed ground you see UNDER, and WALL to buildVolumes() so the range's own roof extends over it rather than a new roof being invented (trap b: change a footprint, never a roof). Pick the range yourself and say why you picked it: the north range is drawn behind the whole garden and the south range is drawn nearest and largest, and that is a real trade you should make with a screenshot, not with an argument. It must be USED: in rain, people in the courtyard should shelter under it rather than only leaving by lawnGate (#179), and a walk under a colonnade is a stop that can perform and say something like every other visit in this town.

queue.brief: The census cannot see winter, and it has been telling the manager the map is flat for 16 iterations partly because of it. #181 added ICE, the 19th tile kind, and `census.mjs` reported unchanged in EVERY field. The cause is deliberate and documented in census.mjs's own comment: all three AGES sit at warmth 0.6929 so that the age axis measures age (the #14 fix), which means no seasonal state exists in any of the nine cells. Give the gate a winter reading. The existing 3 seeds x 3 ages must stay BIT-IDENTICAL and comparable — the baseline travels with the ladder, and breaking that throws away every census row in RUNLOG — so this is an ADDITION, not a re-cut of the ladder. Prove it the way a gate must be proved: pin a 'before' to the REF at #181's commit and show the new reading MOVES across it while the old nine cells do not. Fold in c266 while you are here: seed-identity pins five instants at seed 42 and 125/128 are wet, i.e. seed 42 gets ONE shower in 800 sim s, so its second seed should be chosen FOR its weather and the choice written down.
queue.successLooksLike: `node census.mjs` prints a winter reading beside the summer one; run against the tree at #181 it shows ICE non-zero and tileKinds moving, where the current gate shows nothing. The nine existing cells are byte-identical to today's `census-latest.json`. The ledger says in one line whether `stall.mjs`'s mapFlat now reads the new fields or still cannot.
queue.avoid: Do not change SEEDS or the three AGES, and do not re-pin the baseline in a way that makes today's rows incomparable. Do not turn this into a general census rewrite — one axis, proved against one ref.

queue.brief: The first interaction the sky has ever had in 185 iterations (the column is empty for sky, lane, street and river; interaction is 13 entries in the whole run). The pointer names beds, plots, paving, trees, tenants, faces, roof furniture, allotment furniture, vanes, the mill wheel, the field edge, every bird, every moth and the starlings coming in to roost — and above the horizon it names NOTHING but the murmuration box. Make the sky answer: the moon and its phase, the sun and its hour, the weather the cloud bank is carrying, and the balloon. And the balloon needs the second half of c265 before it can be named honestly. Priced on HEAD: it spawns at x -8 on `day >= 4 && daylight > 0.4 && !raining` at `R() < dt*0.007`, moves at 0.9 cells/s and is deleted only at `x > GW + 8` — 154 cells at 0.9 = 171 sim seconds against a 55 s day, so it is aloft for 3.1 DAYS, across three nights, and it is the night frame's one moving object. Either it comes down or it is explained; a thing you can point at and name is a thing whose day the viewer will notice.
queue.successLooksLike: Pointing anywhere above the horizon returns a name that changes with the hour and the weather, and pointing at the balloon names it. The balloon's time aloft, measured over a seeded year, is a fraction of a day rather than 3.1 days, and a night frame no longer has one unexplained moving object.
queue.avoid: Do not add a second balloon or a fleet; the rarity is the point. Do not hard-code an hour for the descent — a hard-coded HOUR in a light or warmth term is a seasonal bug invisible to a screenshot; solve an hour OF THE SUN. Do not make the naming a tooltip with its own UI: it goes through the one cursor naming path.

queue.brief: The 9th new-CA in 185 iterations and the FIRST in the life domain (c272: new-ca lives in courtyard, lane, street, plaza, river and roofs; after this, sky and the sill are the only domains without one — in a piece subtitled 'a cellular block'). Give the eaves a colony of martins: a per-cell state over the eave line that GROWS, the way `mossCreep` and #181's `stepIce` do, rather than a fixed list of nests placed at build time. A colony is the honest subject for a CA because these birds are colonial — a cell's chance of gaining a nest should read its NEIGHBOURS, so the colony spreads along one house's eave as a front instead of speckling the town uniformly; mud is a weather term, so wet spells build and dry ones do not; and it is seasonal, occupied and busy through the summer and abandoned in autumn. Price the premise first: `roofBirdSpot` and `birds[]` already put birds on roofs, and `nestF` is the ducks' nest on the eyot. A perch is a moment and a nest is FABRIC — say in the ledger how yours differs, or kill the brief and say why.
queue.successLooksLike: Over a seeded year the colony's count rises from 0 in spring to a plateau and empties in autumn, measured by a probe over 4+ seeds and reported as a curve, not a single instant; the nests are CLUSTERED (quote the run-length or nearest-neighbour distance against a uniform control at the same count); and at midsummer the wide shot has birds shuttling to one stretch of eave. Report the colony in `__census` under `structure` so the gate can see it.
queue.avoid: Do not place nests from a constant list — a fixed array is a new-element, not a CA, and the kind is the point. Do not spread them evenly over every house; one uniform hash is a texture, never a PLACE. Do not add a new bird population with its own cap on top of `birds[]` until you have shown the existing one cannot carry it.

queue.brief: c275, promoted. A pane's lamp can go out in the middle of somebody's crossing. `windowLit(sa,sb)` owns bedtime — `windowHours`, HOMES, the miller, the early risers keyed on sunrise — and `paneFigure(sa,sb)` owns the visit, solving `s = (n.t - t0)/(FIG_MIN + FIG_SPAN*hash(...))` over its own window FIG_T0..FIG_T1 clipped to `n.span - 0.8`. Neither asks the other, and `drawPaneFigures` walks LIT_PANES, which is rebuilt each frame from the panes that are lit — so when the lamp goes out under a figure at s = 0.4 the figure does not finish crossing, it ceases. Measure it first (#182's own probe, `probes/pane-figures.mjs`, already reports 1.17 occupied of 13.05 lit and 0 empty nights): count the crossings that are cut short over a seeded year before you fix anything, so the ledger carries the number. Then make the two clocks agree — the cheapest correct fix is for the visit to be offered only inside the lamp's own remaining hours.
queue.successLooksLike: A probe reports the truncation rate on HEAD and 0 after, with occupancy (1.17 of 13.05) and the 52/18/12% at 0/1/2 within noise of #182's numbers — the fix must cost the town almost no figures, and if it costs many, say so and re-price.
queue.avoid: Do not keep a pane lit because somebody is in it — the lamp's clock is the town's bedtime and it wins. Do not give the figure its own persistent object; #182's whole design is that it is solved per frame from `nid` with no anchor that can go stale.
